- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% relative to model output.
- Underestimate late-period prices (last 5–10 days of forecast) when true outcomes show strong upward momentum; adjust upward by 3–7% for the final 10 days.
- When model shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecasted values before final adjustment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Forecast horizon 30d: avoid overconfidence in early days; reduce forecast by 1–2% for each day beyond day 10 if no new data confirms trend.
